title: Act on Management of Disaster Management Resources
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to protect people's lives, physical safety, and property by prescribing matters concerning the management, etc. of disaster management resources, thereby ensuring their systematic and efficient management and their rapid and reliable mobilization where a disaster is likely to occur or has occurred.

Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act mean the following:
1. “Disaster management resources” means material and human resources, such as goods, property, and personnel, necessary for disaster management under Article 3, subparagraph 3 of the Framework Act on the Management of Disasters and Safety (hereinafter referred to as the “Framework Act”) (hereinafter referred to as “disaster management”).
2. “Disaster management goods” means goods falling under any of the following items that are managed as disaster management resources:
(a) Goods under Article 2 (1) of the Goods Management Act;
(b) Goods under Article 2, subparagraph 2 of the Public Property and Goods Management Act;
(c) Other goods equivalent to those under items (a) and (b) that are prescribed by Presidential Decree.
3. “Disaster management property” means property falling under any of the following items that is managed as disaster management resources:
(a) State property falling under Article 5 (1) 1 through 3 of the State Property Act;
(b) Public property falling under Article 4 (1) 1 through 3 of the Public Property and Goods Management Act;
(c) Other property equivalent to that under items (a) and (b) that is prescribed by Presidential Decree.
4. “Disaster management personnel” means persons falling under any of the following items who belong to a management institution under subparagraph 10 or an institution, organization, or corporation with which the head of a management institution has consulted or entered into an agreement in advance under Article 42 (2), and who are managed as disaster management resources:
(a) Persons who have obtained qualifications or licenses under the National Technical Qualifications Act or other statutes (including foreign statutes);
(b) Volunteers under Article 3, subparagraph 2 of the Framework Act on Volunteer Service Activities;
(c) Other persons with extensive knowledge and experience in disaster management.
5. “Supplier” means any of the following:
(a) A person engaged in the business of manufacturing disaster management resources;
(b) A person engaged in the business of selling, lending, or leasing disaster management resources;
(c) A person engaged in the business of providing services that use or utilize disaster management resources.
6. “Supply chain management” means supervising, processing, and managing the series of processes through which disaster management resources or information on such resources are transferred from suppliers to users.
7. “Supply chain management framework” means an interconnected collection of facilities, equipment, information, organizations, personnel, etc. that enables them to function organically with one another for efficient supply chain management activities.
8. “Disaster management logistics” means transport, storage, loading and unloading, etc. carried out from the production or procurement of disaster management resources from suppliers until their delivery to users or recovery from users and disposal, and incidental processing, assembly, classification, repair, packaging, labeling, sales, information and communications, etc.
9. “Disaster management logistics framework” means an interconnected collection of facilities, equipment, information, organizations, personnel, etc. that enables them to function organically with one another for efficient disaster management logistics activities.
10. “Management institution” means any of the following institutions:
(a) A disaster management responsible agency under Article 3, subparagraph 5 of the Framework Act;
(b) A public institution under the Act on the Management of Public Institutions that is prescribed by Presidential Decree for systematic and efficient management of disaster management resources under its jurisdiction;
(c) A local public enterprise under the Local Public Enterprises Act that is prescribed by Presidential Decree for systematic and efficient management of disaster management resources under its jurisdiction.

Article 3 (Duties of the State, etc.)
(1) The State and local governments shall formulate and implement policies necessary for the management of disaster management resources.
(2) Business operators and the public shall actively cooperate with policies concerning the management of disaster management resources implemented by the State or local governments.

Article 4 (Overall Supervision and Coordination of Duties concerning Management of Disaster Management Resources) The Minister of the Interior and Safety shall oversee and coordinate duties concerning the management of disaster management resources performed by the State and local governments.

Article 5 (Relationship with Other Acts)
(1) Except as otherwise expressly provided in other Acts, the management, etc. of disaster management resources shall be governed by this Act.
(2) Matters concerning the management, etc. of disaster management resources not prescribed in this Act shall be governed by other Acts, including the Goods Management Act and the Public Property and Goods Management Act.

CHAPTER II SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT FRAMEWORK AND DISASTER MANAGEMENT LOGISTICS FRAMEWORK

SECTION 1 SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT FRAMEWORK

Article 6 (Establishment of Supply Chain Management Framework)
(1) The Minister of the Interior and Safety shall establish a reliable supply chain management framework for disaster management.
(2) The heads of relevant central administrative agencies may jointly establish with the Minister of the Interior and Safety a supply chain management framework for disaster management resources necessary for disaster management duties under their jurisdiction, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 7 (Surveys of Supply Chain Management Information)
(1) The Minister of the Interior and Safety may survey information necessary for supply chain management prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as the status of suppliers (hereinafter referred to as “supply chain management information”), to establish a supply chain management framework.
(2) The Minister of the Interior and Safety may request any of the following to submit data necessary for a survey under paragraph (1) or directly conduct part of the survey. In such cases, the requested person shall comply unless there are special circumstances:
1. The heads of relevant central administrative agencies;
2. The Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayors, the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Do Governors, and the Special Self-Governing Province Governor (hereinafter referred to as “Mayors/Do Governors”);
3. The heads of Si/Gun/Gu (a head of a Gu means the head of an autonomous Gu; the same applies hereinafter);
4. Business associations of which suppliers are members.

Article 8 (Entry of Supply Chain Management Information)
(1) A person who has surveyed supply chain management information under Article 7 shall enter the survey results in the integrated disaster management resource management system under Article 46.
(2) A supplier falling under either of the following shall enter supply chain management information in the integrated disaster management resource management system under Article 46:
1. A supplier that sells, lends, or leases, or intends to sell, lend, or lease, disaster management resources to management institutions;
2. A supplier that provides or intends to provide management institutions with services using or utilizing disaster management resources.

Article 9 (Designation of National Disaster Management Support Enterprises)
(1) Where deemed necessary for the smooth establishment of a supply chain management framework and disaster management at the national level, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may designate as a national disaster management support enterprise a supplier that has consented in advance to duties under paragraph (2), from among suppliers. In such cases, fair and transparent procedures, methods, and criteria shall be followed, and the designation shall be disclosed.
(2) The Minister of the Interior and Safety shall serve a notice (including electronic service; the same applies hereinafter) specifying duties concerning the management and mobilization of disaster management resources arising from the designation on a national disaster management support enterprise designated under paragraph (1) (hereinafter referred to as a “national disaster management support enterprise”).
(3) A national disaster management support enterprise may affix to or use on disaster management resources, etc. a mark indicating its status as such an enterprise, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety.
(4) A person other than a national disaster management support enterprise shall not use that name or a similar name.
(5) Other specific matters necessary for the designation, etc. of national disaster management support enterprises shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 10 (Preparatory Measures for National Disaster Management Support Enterprises)
(1) As prescribed by Presidential Decree, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may order a national disaster management support enterprise to take the following preparatory measures within the scope necessary to perform duties concerning the management and mobilization of disaster management resources, taking account of its capacity to bear the burden:
1. Reinforcement or expansion of facilities;
2. Development of technology;
3. Establishment of a supply chain management system and linkage with the integrated disaster management resource management system under Article 46.
(2) When intending to issue an order for preparatory measures under paragraph (1), the Minister of the Interior and Safety shall consult with or hear the opinion of the relevant national disaster management support enterprise in advance.
(3) The Minister of the Interior and Safety may provide administrative and financial support to a national disaster management support enterprise that complies with an order for preparatory measures under paragraph (1).

Article 11 (Cancellation of Designation of National Disaster Management Support Enterprises)
(1) Where grounds prescribed by Presidential Decree occur, such as closure of business, insolvency, or violation of this Act or an order under this Act by a national disaster management support enterprise, and the Minister of the Interior and Safety deems that it is unable to perform its duties, the Minister shall cancel its designation.
(2) Upon cancelling a designation under paragraph (1), the Minister of the Interior and Safety shall notify the relevant supplier of that fact in writing without delay.

Article 12 (Designation of Regional Disaster Management Support Enterprises)
(1) Where deemed necessary for disaster management within the relevant jurisdiction, a Mayor/Do Governor may, after consultation with the Minister of the Interior and Safety, designate as a disaster management support enterprise for that jurisdiction a supplier located within the jurisdiction that has consented in advance to duties under paragraph (2). In such cases, fair and transparent procedures, methods, and criteria shall be followed, and the designation shall be disclosed.
(2) A Mayor/Do Governor shall serve on a disaster management support enterprise for the relevant jurisdiction designated under paragraph (1) (hereinafter referred to as a “regional disaster management support enterprise”) a notice specifying duties concerning the management and mobilization of disaster management resources arising from the designation, and notify the Minister of the Interior and Safety of the designation in writing.
(3) A regional disaster management support enterprise may affix to or use on the relevant disaster management resources, etc. a mark indicating its status as such an enterprise, as prescribed by ordinance of the Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, Do, or Special Self-Governing Province (hereinafter referred to as “Si/Do”).
(4) A person other than a regional disaster management support enterprise shall not use that name or a similar name.
(5) Other specific matters necessary for the designation, etc. of regional disaster management support enterprises shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 13 (Preparatory Measures for Regional Disaster Management Support Enterprises)
(1) As prescribed by Presidential Decree, a Mayor/Do Governor may order a regional disaster management support enterprise to take the following preparatory measures within the scope necessary to perform duties concerning the management and mobilization of disaster management resources, taking account of its capacity to bear the burden:
1. Reinforcement or expansion of facilities;
2. Development of technology;
3. Establishment of a supply chain management system and linkage with the integrated disaster management resource management system under Article 46.
(2) When intending to issue an order for preparatory measures under paragraph (1), a Mayor/Do Governor shall consult with or hear the opinion of the relevant regional disaster management support enterprise in advance.
(3) A Mayor/Do Governor may provide administrative and financial support to a regional disaster management support enterprise that complies with an order for preparatory measures under paragraph (1).

Article 14 (Cancellation of Designation of Regional Disaster Management Support Enterprises)
(1) Where grounds prescribed by Presidential Decree occur, such as closure of business, insolvency, or violation of this Act or an order under this Act by a regional disaster management support enterprise, and a Mayor/Do Governor deems that it is unable to perform duties concerning the management and mobilization of disaster management resources, the Mayor/Do Governor shall cancel its designation.
(2) When intending to cancel a designation under paragraph (1), a Mayor/Do Governor shall consult with the Minister of the Interior and Safety in advance.
(3) Upon cancelling a designation under paragraph (1), a Mayor/Do Governor shall notify the relevant supplier and the Minister of the Interior and Safety of that fact in writing without delay.

Article 15 (Export Prohibitions)
(1) Where a sharp increase in the price of disaster management resources or a shortage of supply is likely to seriously undermine public safety, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may prohibit their export or removal from the country.
(2) To impose a prohibition under paragraph (1), the Minister of the Interior and Safety shall consult with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies in advance and determine and publicly announce the period of prohibition in advance.

SECTION 2 DISASTER MANAGEMENT LOGISTICS FRAMEWORK

Article 16 (Establishment of Disaster Management Logistics Framework)
(1) The Minister of the Interior and Safety shall establish a reliable disaster management logistics framework by utilizing the logistics frameworks of persons engaged in logistics business under Article 2 (1) 2 of the Framework Act on Logistics Policies (hereinafter referred to as “logistics enterprises”) for smooth supply and mobilization of disaster management resources.
(2) When establishing a disaster management logistics framework, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may consult with or hear the opinions of the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, or the Minister of Trade and Industry in advance. <Amended 2025.10.1>

Article 17 (Designation of National Disaster Management Logistics Enterprises)
(1) Where deemed necessary for the smooth establishment of a disaster management logistics framework and disaster management at the national level, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may designate as a national disaster management logistics enterprise a logistics enterprise that has consented in advance to duties under paragraph (2), from among logistics enterprises. In such cases, fair and transparent procedures, methods, and criteria shall be followed, and the designation shall be disclosed.
(2) The Minister of the Interior and Safety shall serve on a national disaster management logistics enterprise designated under paragraph (1) (hereinafter referred to as a “national disaster management logistics enterprise”) a notice specifying duties concerning disaster management logistics arising from the designation.
(3) A national disaster management logistics enterprise may affix to or use on means of transport, etc. a mark indicating its status as such an enterprise, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety.
(4) A person other than a national disaster management logistics enterprise shall not use that name or a similar name.
(5) Other specific matters necessary for the designation, etc. of national disaster management logistics enterprises shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 18 (Preparatory Measures for National Disaster Management Logistics Enterprises)
(1) As prescribed by Presidential Decree, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may order a national disaster management logistics enterprise to take the following preparatory measures within the scope necessary to perform duties concerning disaster management logistics, taking account of its capacity to bear the burden:
1. Expansion of logistics facilities and equipment necessary for efficient disaster management logistics activities;
2. Linkage of major logistics facilities with means of transport;
3. Promotion of joint operation of disaster management logistics;
4. Establishment of a disaster management logistics system and linkage with the integrated disaster management resource management system under Article 46.
(2) When intending to issue an order for preparatory measures under paragraph (1), the Minister of the Interior and Safety shall consult with or hear the opinion of the relevant national disaster management logistics enterprise in advance.
(3) The Minister of the Interior and Safety may provide administrative and financial support to a national disaster management logistics enterprise that complies with an order for preparatory measures under paragraph (1).

Article 19 (Cancellation of Designation of National Disaster Management Logistics Enterprises)
(1) Where grounds prescribed by Presidential Decree occur, such as closure of business, insolvency, or violation of this Act or an order under this Act by a national disaster management logistics enterprise, and the Minister of the Interior and Safety deems that it is unable to perform duties concerning disaster management logistics, the Minister shall cancel its designation.
(2) Upon cancelling a designation under paragraph (1), the Minister of the Interior and Safety shall notify the relevant logistics enterprise of that fact in writing without delay.

CHAPTER III PERSONNEL FOR MANAGEMENT OF DISASTER MANAGEMENT RESOURCES

Article 20 (Resource Management Officers)
(1) The head of a management institution may delegate affairs concerning the management of disaster management resources under the head's jurisdiction to public officials or employees belonging to the institution (hereinafter referred to as “public officials, etc.”), and, where necessary, to public officials, etc. belonging to another management institution, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Public officials, etc. to whom affairs concerning the management of disaster management resources are delegated under paragraph (1) shall be referred to as resource management officers.
(3) Delegation of affairs concerning the management of disaster management resources under paragraph (1) may be effected by designating a specific position.
(4) Upon being delegated affairs concerning the management of disaster management resources under paragraph (1), a resource management officer shall enter basic information about the officer, including the management institution and department to which the officer belongs and contact details, in the integrated disaster management resource management system under Article 46 without delay.

Article 21 (Resource Receipt and Issue Officers)
(1) As prescribed by Presidential Decree, a resource management officer (including public officials, etc. assigned responsibility for part of the officer's affairs under Article 23 (1); the same applies hereinafter) shall delegate affairs concerning the receipt, issue, and storage of disaster management resources (excluding affairs concerning orders for receipt and issue) to public officials, etc. of the management institution to which the officer belongs.
(2) Public officials, etc. to whom affairs concerning the receipt, issue, and storage of disaster management resources are delegated under paragraph (1) shall be referred to as resource receipt and issue officers.
(3) Delegation of affairs concerning the receipt, issue, and storage of disaster management resources under paragraph (1) may be effected by designating a specific position.
(4) Upon being delegated affairs concerning the receipt, issue, and storage of disaster management resources under paragraph (1), a resource receipt and issue officer shall enter basic information about the officer, including the management institution and department to which the officer belongs and contact details, in the integrated disaster management resource management system under Article 46 without delay.

Article 22 (Resource Utilization Officers)
(1) As prescribed by Presidential Decree, a resource management officer shall have public officials, etc. of the management institution to which the officer belongs use or utilize disaster management resources according to the purposes and uses of disaster management duties, or delegate to them affairs concerning the management of disaster management resources in use or being utilized (hereinafter referred to as “affairs concerning the use and utilization of disaster management resources”).
(2) Public officials, etc. to whom affairs concerning the use and utilization of disaster management resources are delegated shall be referred to as resource utilization officers.
(3) Delegation of affairs concerning the use and utilization of disaster management resources may be effected by designating a specific position.
(4) Upon being delegated affairs concerning the use and utilization of disaster management resources, a resource utilization officer shall enter basic information about the officer, including the management institution and department to which the officer belongs and contact details, in the integrated disaster management resource management system under Article 46 without delay.

Article 23 (Division of Duties and Acting Arrangements in Management Institutions)
(1) The head of a management institution may appoint public officials, etc. to take responsibility for part of the affairs of a resource management officer, and a resource management officer may appoint public officials, etc. to take responsibility for part of the affairs of a resource receipt and issue officer, respectively, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Where a resource management officer is unable to perform duties for unavoidable reasons, the head of the management institution may designate public officials, etc. to act for that officer; where a resource receipt and issue officer or resource utilization officer is unable to perform duties for unavoidable reasons, a resource management officer may designate public officials, etc. to act for that officer, respectively, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) Public officials, etc. assigned part of the duties and public officials, etc. designated to act under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall enter basic information about themselves, including the management institution and department to which they belong and contact details, in the integrated disaster management resource management system under Article 46 without delay.

Article 24 (Education of Resource Management Officers)
(1) Resource management officers, resource receipt and issue officers, and resource utilization officers (including public officials, etc. assigned part of the duties or designated to act under Article 23 (1) and (2); the same applies hereinafter) shall receive specialized education concerning the management of disaster management resources conducted by the Minister of the Interior and Safety (hereinafter referred to as “specialized education”), regularly or from time to time.
(2) The Minister of the Interior and Safety may request the head of the management institution to which a person belongs to discipline that person for failing to receive specialized education without just cause.
(3) A person who has received specialized education shall be deemed to have received specialized education under Article 29-2 (1) of the Framework Act.
(4) The types, recipients, and intervals of specialized education and other matters necessary therefor, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (3), shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety.

CHAPTER IV MANAGEMENT OF DISASTER MANAGEMENT GOODS

SECTION 1 GENERAL RULES ON DISASTER MANAGEMENT GOODS

Article 25 (Classification of Disaster Management Goods)
(1) The head of a management institution shall classify disaster management goods under the head's jurisdiction by use, function, nature, and item, and manage them efficiently and appropriately.
(2) Where deemed necessary for efficient use and disposal of disaster management goods under the head's jurisdiction, the head of a management institution may change the classification to which those goods belong.
(3) Classification criteria for disaster management goods, changes in their classification under paragraphs (1) and (2), and other matters necessary for the classification of disaster management resources shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 26 (Standardization of Disaster Management Goods)
(1) The head of a management institution shall establish standards for disaster management goods used only by that institution and its affiliated institutions and subordinate institutions, organizations, and corporations (hereinafter referred to as “affiliated and subordinate institutions, etc.”).
(2) The Minister of the Interior and Safety shall establish standards for disaster management goods commonly used by management institutions.
(3) Matters necessary for establishing standards under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 27 (Consultation on Matters concerning Disaster Management Goods) To manage disaster management goods efficiently and appropriately, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may cooperate with the Administrator of the Public Procurement Service by consulting on the following matters, sharing related information, or other means:
1. Matters concerning standards for disaster management goods under Article 26;
2. Matters concerning stockpile management standards for disaster management goods under Article 29;
3. Matters concerning establishment of the integrated disaster management resource management system under Article 46;
4. Other matters concerning the management of disaster management goods, such as supply chain management, on which mutual cooperation is deemed necessary.

SECTION 2 STOCKPILING AND MANAGEMENT OF DISASTER MANAGEMENT GOODS

Article 28 (Stockpile Management Plans for Disaster Management Goods)
(1) The head of a management institution shall formulate an annual stockpile management plan for disaster management goods under the head's jurisdiction and submit it to the head of the institution according to the following classifications, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such cases, the heads of central administrative agencies and Mayors/Do Governors shall compile the submitted stockpile management plans for disaster management goods and submit them to the Minister of the Interior and Safety:
1. Central administrative agency: The Minister of the Interior and Safety;
2. Affiliated and subordinate institutions, etc. of a central administrative agency: The head of the competent central administrative agency;
3. Si/Do: The Minister of the Interior and Safety;
4. Si/Gun/Gu (a Gu means an autonomous Gu; the same applies hereinafter): The competent Mayor/Do Governor;
5. Affiliated and subordinate institutions, etc. of a local government: The head of the competent local government.
(2) A resource management officer shall stockpile and manage disaster management goods under the officer's jurisdiction according to the stockpile management plan for disaster management goods formulated under paragraph (1).
(3) Resource management officers, resource receipt and issue officers, and resource utilization officers shall record and maintain matters necessary for stockpiling and managing disaster management goods in standard forms (meaning input/output data forms of the integrated disaster management resource management system under Article 46), as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety.

Article 29 (Stockpile Management Standards for Disaster Management Goods)
(1) The Minister of the Interior and Safety shall establish the following standards for major disaster management goods (hereinafter referred to as “stockpile management standards”) and notify the heads of management institutions thereof, as prescribed by Presidential Decree:
1. Criteria for setting standard quantities;
2. Useful lives;
3. Inventory management standards;
4. Other standards determined by the Minister of the Interior and Safety to be necessary for stockpiling and managing major disaster management goods.
(2) The head of a management institution shall independently establish and operate stockpile management standards for disaster management goods for which such standards have not been established. In such cases, information on those standards shall be entered in the integrated disaster management resource management system under Article 46.
(3) A resource management officer shall, with the approval of the head of the management institution to which the officer belongs, stockpile and manage disaster management goods under the officer's jurisdiction according to the stockpile management standards.
(4) In either of the following cases, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may adjust the stockpile management standards as prescribed by Presidential Decree:
1. Where the head of a management institution requests adjustment of the stockpile management standards;
2. Where the Minister of the Interior and Safety deems adjustment of the stockpile management standards necessary.
(5) To establish stockpile management standards, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may have the head of an affiliated institution prescribed by Presidential Decree that is responsible for matters concerning research and development of disaster and safety policies and related technology research and develop those standards.

Article 30 (Inventory Surveys of Disaster Management Goods)
(1) The head of a management institution shall conduct inventory surveys of disaster management goods stockpiled and managed, regularly or from time to time, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, and submit a report on the survey results to the head of the institution according to the classifications in Article 28 (1).
(2) The Minister of the Interior and Safety and Mayors/Do Governors may conduct special inventory surveys of disaster management goods of management institutions, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such cases, a special inventory survey by a Mayor/Do Governor shall be limited to disaster management goods of Si/Gun/Gu within the relevant jurisdiction and affiliated and subordinate institutions, etc.
(3) Where the head of a management institution, the Minister of the Interior and Safety, or a Mayor/Do Governor discovers damage to or loss of disaster management goods as a result of an inventory survey or special inventory survey under paragraph (1) or the former part of paragraph (2), the result of handling the matter shall be notified to the Board of Audit and Inspection in writing without delay: Provided, That this shall not apply to a management institution that is not subject to audit or inspection by the Board under the Board of Audit and Inspection Act.
(4) Where an increase or decrease in disaster management goods is found as a result of an inventory survey or special inventory survey under paragraph (1) or the former part of paragraph (2), and its cause is clearly an administrative error, the head of a management institution may make an adjustment as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(5) Where deemed necessary for efficient use, disposal, etc. of disaster management goods, a resource management officer may transfer disaster management goods under the officer's jurisdiction to the jurisdiction of another resource management officer, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 31 (Maintenance of Disaster Management Goods) A resource management officer shall select major disaster management goods subject to maintenance and maintain them according to maintenance standards, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

SECTION 3 ACQUISITION, STORAGE, AND USE OF DISASTER MANAGEMENT GOODS

Article 32 (Acquisition of Disaster Management Goods)
(1) A resource management officer shall request public officials, etc. in charge of contracts to take measures necessary for acquiring disaster management goods, within the scope of the stockpile management plan formulated under Article 28 (1) for goods specified in that plan, and whenever needed for other disaster management goods, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Where a disaster is likely to occur or has occurred and the resource management officer deems it necessary for urgent preparedness, response, recovery, etc., the officer may request public officials, etc. in charge of contracts to preferentially acquire disaster management goods of a national disaster management support enterprise or a regional disaster management support enterprise by negotiated contract. In such cases, procedures and methods for negotiated contracts, etc. shall follow relevant statutes, including the Act on Contracts to Which the State Is a Party and the Act on Contracts to Which a Local Government Is a Party.
(3) Upon receiving a request under paragraphs (1) and (2), public officials, etc. in charge of contracts shall take measures necessary for acquiring the relevant disaster management goods within budgetary limits, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(4) Disaster management goods shall not be acquired without acceptance inspection by relevant public officials, etc. or technicians appointed by the head of the management institution or public officials, etc. delegated by that head: Provided, That this shall not apply where the goods are for emergency measures under Article 37 of the Framework Act.
(5) Where a resource management officer intends to purchase disaster management goods and another resource management officer is inquiring whether other institutions wish to acquire disaster management goods of the same name for transfer of management, and the officer judges that the goods under inquiry can achieve the project purpose for disaster management, the officer shall acquire the goods under inquiry through transfer of management.

Article 33 (Principles for Storage and Receipt and Issue of Disaster Management Goods)
(1) A resource management officer shall store disaster management goods in stockpile facilities prescribed by Presidential Decree that belong to the management institution to which the officer belongs, so that the goods are available for use or disposal at all times: Provided, That where storage in such stockpile facilities is deemed unsuitable for use or disposal of the goods, or another special reason exists, the goods may be stored in any of the following facilities or warehouses:
1. Stockpile facilities of another management institution;
2. Logistics facilities or logistics warehouses of a national disaster management support enterprise or a regional disaster management support enterprise;
3. Logistics facilities or logistics warehouses of a national disaster management logistics enterprise;
4. Other facilities or warehouses approved by the head of the management institution to which the officer belongs.
(2) To have disaster management goods received or issued, a resource management officer shall order the resource receipt and issue officer to receive or issue them, clearly specifying their classification.
(3) A resource receipt and issue officer shall not receive or issue disaster management goods without an order under paragraph (2).
(4) Where a resource receipt and issue officer deems that any disaster management goods stored in stockpile facilities, etc. under paragraph (1) (excluding goods returned pursuant to an order under Article 34 (3)) cannot be used or require repair or modification, the officer shall report that fact to the resource management officer.
(5) Where a resource management officer deems, based on a report under paragraph (4) or Article 34 (2), that disaster management goods require repair or modification, the officer shall request public officials, etc. in charge of contracts or other relevant public officials, etc. to take the measures necessary for such repair or modification.
(6) Matters necessary for storage, receipt and issue, and measures for repair or modification of disaster management goods, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (5), shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 34 (Use and Return of Disaster Management Goods)
(1) When ordering the receipt or issue of disaster management goods for use, a resource management officer shall clearly specify the purpose of use and notify the resource utilization officer of that fact: Provided, That this shall not apply where an order for receipt or issue is made at the request of the resource utilization officer.
(2) Where any disaster management goods in use are no longer needed, cannot be used, or require repair or modification, a resource utilization officer shall report that fact to the resource management officer.
(3) Upon receiving a report under paragraph (2), the resource management officer shall verify the facts and, if the goods are found to fall within that paragraph, order the resource utilization officer to return them.

SECTION 4 DISPOSAL OF DISASTER MANAGEMENT GOODS

Article 35 (Exchange and Lending of Disaster Management Goods)
(1) Where deemed necessary for efficient management of disaster management goods, the head of a management institution may exchange disaster management goods with goods owned by the head of another management institution, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Disaster management goods shall not be lent: Provided, That this shall not apply where the goods support the disaster management duties of another management institution.
(3) Where the head of a management institution lends disaster management goods to support the disaster management duties of another management institution under the proviso to paragraph (2), the lending may be without charge.

Article 36 (Determination of Disaster Management Goods as Unneeded)
(1) Where any disaster management goods under a resource management officer's jurisdiction are no longer needed or cannot be used (including goods mobilized under Articles 50 through 52), the officer shall determine those goods to be unneeded: Provided, That approval from the head of the management institution to which the officer belongs shall be obtained for disaster management goods prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Where disaster management goods determined to be unneeded under paragraph (1) (hereinafter referred to as “unneeded goods”) fall under any of the following, a resource management officer may discard them: Provided, That approval from the head of the management institution to which the officer belongs shall be obtained for disaster management goods prescribed by Presidential Decree.
1. Where they are unsuitable for sale;
2. Where their sale is deemed disadvantageous to the State, a local government, or a management institution;
3. Where they cannot be sold.
(3) Criteria for determining goods to be unneeded under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety.

Article 37 (Sale of Disaster Management Goods)
(1) Disaster management goods shall not be sold: Provided, That disaster management goods intended for sale and unneeded goods may be sold.
(2) For disaster management goods or unneeded goods under the proviso to paragraph (1) that remain unsold, the head of a management institution or the Administrator of the Public Procurement Service may apply special sale provisions as prescribed by Presidential Decree, notwithstanding the Act on Contracts to Which the State Is a Party and the Act on Contracts to Which a Local Government Is a Party.

Article 38 (Requests for Sale of Unneeded Goods)
(1) The head of a management institution may request the Administrator of the Public Procurement Service to sell unneeded goods that can be utilized.
(2) Where unneeded goods that can be utilized have not been disposed of through transfer of management, sale, etc., the head of a management institution may transfer their management to the Administrator of the Public Procurement Service without consideration.
(3) The Administrator of the Public Procurement Service shall manage, repair, and dispose of unneeded goods whose management has been transferred without consideration under paragraph (2), as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 39 (Gratuitous Transfer of Unneeded Goods)
(1) Where deemed necessary for utilization of unneeded goods, the head of a management institution may transfer the relevant disaster management goods without consideration to any of the following, as prescribed by Presidential Decree:
1. Another management institution;
2. Educational and research institutions and nonprofit corporations prescribed by Presidential Decree;
3. Other persons prescribed by Presidential Decree who are members of safety-vulnerable groups under Article 3, subparagraph 9-3 of the Framework Act.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), disaster management goods acquired for provision to the general public for disaster management may be transferred to the general public without consideration.

Article 40 (Handling of Lost or Damaged Disaster Management Goods)
(1) Where the head of a management institution discovers loss of or damage to disaster management goods as a result of an inventory survey or special inventory survey under Article 30 (1) or the former part of Article 30 (2), the head may issue an order for reimbursement under Article 6 (1) of the Act on the Liability of Accounting Personnel, etc., as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) The head of a management institution shall not issue an order for reimbursement for damage to disaster management goods arising from reasonable causes related to disaster management duties.

CHAPTER V MANAGEMENT OF DISASTER MANAGEMENT PROPERTY AND DISASTER MANAGEMENT PERSONNEL

Article 41 (Management Plans for Disaster Management Property)
(1) The head of a management institution shall formulate an annual management plan for disaster management property under the head's jurisdiction and submit it to the head of the institution according to the classifications in Article 28 (1), as prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such cases, the heads of central administrative agencies and Mayors/Do Governors shall compile the submitted management plans for disaster management property and submit them to the Minister of the Interior and Safety.
(2) A resource management officer shall manage disaster management property under the officer's jurisdiction according to the management plan for disaster management property formulated under paragraph (1).
(3) Resource management officers, resource receipt and issue officers, and resource utilization officers shall record and maintain matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as the types and history of use of disaster management property managed under paragraph (2), using the integrated disaster management resource management system under Article 46.

Article 42 (Principles for Management of Disaster Management Personnel)
(1) Disaster management personnel shall be managed by the institution, organization, or corporation to which they belong.
(2) The head of a management institution shall secure disaster management personnel for disaster management duties under the head's jurisdiction through prior consultation or agreements with institutions, organizations, or corporations to which disaster management personnel falling under any item of Article 2, subparagraph 4 belong.
(3) Where deemed necessary for disaster management duties under the head's jurisdiction, the head of a management institution may provide education and training to disaster management personnel managed by that head. In such cases, the head of the management institution shall bear the costs of the education and training.

Article 43 (Management Plans for Disaster Management Personnel)
(1) The head of a management institution shall formulate a management plan for disaster management personnel under the head's jurisdiction and submit it to the head of the institution according to the classifications in Article 28 (1), as prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such cases, the heads of central administrative agencies and Mayors/Do Governors shall compile the submitted management plans for disaster management personnel and submit them to the Minister of the Interior and Safety.
(2) A resource management officer shall manage disaster management personnel under the officer's jurisdiction according to the management plan for disaster management personnel formulated under paragraph (1).
(3) A resource management officer shall record and maintain matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as the contact details of institutions, organizations, or corporations to which disaster management personnel managed under paragraph (2) belong and their mobilization history, using the integrated disaster management resource management system under Article 46.

CHAPTER VI INTEGRATED MANAGEMENT OF DISASTER MANAGEMENT RESOURCES

Article 44 (Integrated Management of Disaster Management Resources in Si/Do)
(1) A Mayor/Do Governor may manage disaster management resources within the relevant jurisdiction in an integrated manner through consultation with the heads of Si/Gun/Gu within that jurisdiction.
(2) When managing disaster management resources within the relevant jurisdiction in an integrated manner under paragraph (1), a Mayor/Do Governor shall reflect the details thereof in the following plans. The same applies to the heads of Si/Gun/Gu:
1. Stockpile management plans for disaster management goods under Article 28;
2. Management plans for disaster management property under Article 41;
3. Management plans for disaster management personnel under Article 43.
(3) When managing disaster management resources within the relevant jurisdiction in an integrated manner under paragraph (1), a Mayor/Do Governor shall establish an organization dedicated to the integrated management duties.
(4) Matters necessary for the composition, etc. of the dedicated organization under paragraph (3) shall be prescribed by Si/Do ordinance.

Article 45 (Establishment and Operation of Regional Integrated Disaster Management Resource Management Centers)
(1) When managing disaster management resources within the relevant jurisdiction in an integrated manner under Article 44 (1), a Mayor/Do Governor shall establish and operate a regional integrated disaster management resource management center (hereinafter referred to as a “regional integrated resource management center”), as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) The Minister of the Interior and Safety and the heads of relevant central administrative agencies may provide administrative and financial support necessary for establishing and operating regional integrated resource management centers (including gratuitous transfer of disaster management goods).
(3) Where deemed necessary for efficient establishment and operation of a regional integrated resource management center, a Mayor/Do Governor may have a national disaster management logistics enterprise perform such duties on the Mayor/Do Governor's behalf, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(4) A Mayor/Do Governor may jointly use disaster management goods stored in the stockpile facilities of a regional integrated resource management center with the heads of Si/Gun/Gu within the relevant jurisdiction or the heads of affiliated and subordinate institutions, etc.
(5) Matters necessary for establishment, operation, and performance of duties on behalf of another for regional integrated resource management centers, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (4), shall be prescribed by Si/Do ordinance.

Article 46 (Establishment and Operation of Integrated Disaster Management Resource Management System)
(1) The Minister of the Interior and Safety may establish and operate an integrated disaster management resource management system (hereinafter referred to as “integrated resource management system”) to manage the following information related to disaster management resources:
1. Information on establishment of supply chain management frameworks and disaster management logistics frameworks;
2. The status of designation of national disaster management support enterprises;
3. The status of designation of regional disaster management support enterprises;
4. The status of designation of national disaster management logistics enterprises;
5. Information on resource management officers, resource receipt and issue officers, and resource utilization officers;
6. The status of persons subject to and completing specialized education;
7. Information on the history of management of disaster management goods;
8. Information on the history of management of disaster management property;
9. Information on the history of management of disaster management personnel;
10. Information on the history of mobilization of disaster management resources;
11. Other information related to disaster management resources prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety.
(2) Where deemed necessary for establishing and operating the integrated resource management system, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may request suppliers, logistics enterprises, management institutions, and relevant administrative agencies to submit data necessary for its establishment and operation. In such cases, a person receiving a request shall comply unless there is a special reason not to do so.
(3) The Minister of the Interior and Safety may provide information in the integrated resource management system to national disaster management support enterprises, national disaster management logistics enterprises, regional disaster management support enterprises, management institutions, relevant administrative agencies, etc., or, where necessary, disclose part of the information to the general public.
(4) Matters necessary for establishing and operating the integrated resource management system, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (3), shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 47 (Establishment and Operation of National Information Center for Integrated Management of Disaster Management Resources)
(1) The Minister of the Interior and Safety may establish and operate the National Information Center for Integrated Management of Disaster Management Resources (hereinafter referred to as “National Integrated Resource Management Information Center”) to establish and operate the integrated resource management system and an integrated management information framework for processing, accumulating, and providing information on disaster management resources.
(2) Where deemed necessary, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may designate any of the following institutions or organizations as the institution operating the National Integrated Resource Management Information Center, as prescribed by Presidential Decree:
1. A public institution prescribed by Presidential Decree;
2. A government-funded research institution under the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Research Institutions or the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Science and Technology Research Institutions;
3. A nonprofit institution or organization possessing qualifications prescribed by Presidential Decree, including capital, equipment, and personnel.
(3) The Minister of the Interior and Safety may provide administrative and financial support necessary to enable an institution or organization designated under paragraph (2) as the institution operating the National Integrated Resource Management Information Center (hereinafter referred to as “information center operating institution”) to operate the Center smoothly.

Article 48 (Revocation of Designation of Information Center Operating Institutions) The Minister of the Interior and Safety may revoke the designation of an information center operating institution in any of the following cases: Provided, That designation shall be revoked in the case of subparagraph 1.
1. Where designation was obtained by fraud or other improper means;
2. Where the institution no longer possesses the qualifications under Article 47 (2) 3;
3. Where information in the integrated resource management system has been used for profit-making purposes;
4. Where the Minister of the Interior and Safety otherwise deems the institution unable to perform duties concerning operation of the National Integrated Resource Management Information Center, including violation of this Act or standards under this Act or neglect of duties.

CHAPTER VII MOBILIZATION OF DISASTER MANAGEMENT RESOURCES

Article 49 (Measures for Mobilization of Disaster Management Resources) Where a disaster is likely to occur or has occurred, the head of a management institution shall mobilize disaster management resources under the head's jurisdiction without delay or take measures necessary to comply with mobilization orders under Articles 50 through 52.

Article 50 (Mobilization Orders by Mayors/Do Governors)
(1) Where a Mayor/Do Governor (meaning the head of the relevant headquarters where Si/Do disaster and safety countermeasures headquarters under Article 16 (1) of the Framework Act is in operation; the same applies in this Article and Article 51) deems that a disaster has occurred or is likely to occur within the relevant jurisdiction, the Mayor/Do Governor may order any of the following to mobilize disaster management resources, as prescribed by Presidential Decree:
1. A person operating a regional integrated resource management center on behalf of another under Article 45 (3);
2. Regional disaster management support enterprises under the Mayor/Do Governor's jurisdiction;
3. The heads of management institutions within the relevant jurisdiction (excluding central administrative agencies and their affiliated and subordinate institutions, etc.; the same applies in Article 59 (2)).
(2) Where disaster management duties cannot be performed, or are difficult to perform, at Si/Gun/Gu level, the head of a Si/Gun/Gu (meaning the head of the relevant headquarters where Si/Gun/Gu disaster and safety countermeasures headquarters under Article 16 (1) of the Framework Act is in operation) may request the Mayor/Do Governor to provide disaster management resources. In such cases, the Mayor/Do Governor receiving the request shall provide disaster management resources, including by issuing a mobilization order under paragraph (1), unless there is a special reason not to do so.

Article 51 (Mobilization Orders by Head of Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters)
(1) In any of the following cases, the head of the Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters under Article 14 (1) of the Framework Act (hereinafter referred to as “head of the Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters”) may order national disaster management support enterprises, national disaster management logistics enterprises, and the heads of management institutions to mobilize disaster management resources, as prescribed by Presidential Decree:
1. Where a large-scale disaster under Article 14 (1) of the Framework Act is deemed to have occurred or be likely to occur;
2. Where support for the disaster management duties of a Mayor/Do Governor is deemed necessary.
(2) Where disaster management duties cannot be performed, or are difficult to perform, at Si/Do level, a Mayor/Do Governor may request the head of the Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters to provide disaster management resources. In such cases, the head receiving the request shall provide disaster management resources, including by issuing a mobilization order under paragraph (1), unless there is a special reason not to do so.

Article 52 (Mobilization Orders by Head of Central Accident Response Headquarters) Where deemed necessary for disaster management at the national level in the relevant field, the head of the Central Accident Response Headquarters under Article 15-2 (1) of the Framework Act may, through consultation with the Minister of the Interior and Safety, order national disaster management support enterprises, national disaster management logistics enterprises, and the heads of management institutions to mobilize disaster management resources, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 53 (Principle of Bearing Costs)
(1) Costs incurred in mobilizing disaster management resources under Articles 50 through 52 shall be borne by the person obligated to bear costs necessary for disaster management, etc. under Article 62 (1) of the Framework Act: Provided, That costs for disaster management resources managed by the head of a management institution may be borne by that head.
(2) Costs under the main clause of paragraph (1) shall be settled afterward according to criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) Where deemed necessary for disaster management at the national level, the State may bear all or part of the costs under the main clause of paragraph (1).
(4) Where deemed necessary for disaster management within the relevant jurisdiction, the head of a local government may bear all or part of the costs under the main clause of paragraph (1).

Article 54 (Compensation for Loss, Medical Treatment, etc.)
(1) Articles 64 and 65 of the Framework Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to compensation for loss arising from mobilization under Articles 49 through 52 and to medical treatment and compensation, etc. for persons who die or are injured (including persons who die or become disabled due to an injury).
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), where other statutes, such as the Infectious Disease Control and Prevention Act, prescribe matters concerning compensation for loss, medical treatment, etc. related to mobilization, those provisions may apply mutatis mutandis.

Article 55 (Mobilization Exercises for Disaster Management Resources)
(1) The Minister of the Interior and Safety and Mayors/Do Governors shall conduct exercises concerning mobilization of disaster management resources (hereinafter referred to as “mobilization exercises”) at least once each year.
(2) The Minister of the Interior and Safety and Mayors/Do Governors may conduct mobilization exercises in conjunction with disaster preparedness exercises under Article 35 of the Framework Act.
(3) National disaster management support enterprises, regional disaster management support enterprises, national disaster management logistics enterprises, information center operating institutions, and the heads of management institutions shall participate in mobilization exercises unless there is a special reason not to do so.
(4) Matters necessary for the methods and procedures, etc. of mobilization exercises, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (3), shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER VIII SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 56 (Duties of Lead Disaster Management Agencies)
(1) The head of a lead disaster management agency under Article 3, subparagraph 5-2 of the Framework Act (hereinafter referred to as “lead disaster management agency”) shall, regularly or from time to time, survey material and human resources that need to be managed as disaster management goods, disaster management property, or disaster management personnel for disaster management in the relevant field and notify the Minister of the Interior and Safety thereof, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) The head of a lead disaster management agency may request any of the following to submit data necessary for a survey under paragraph (1). In such cases, a person receiving a request shall comply unless there is a special reason not to do so:
1. The heads of relevant central administrative agencies;
2. The heads of local governments;
3. Suppliers;
4. Logistics enterprises;
5. Other institutions, organizations, or corporations related to disaster management resources.
(3) Where deemed necessary for efficient conduct of a survey under paragraph (1), the head of a lead disaster management agency may have a specialized institution conduct all or part of the survey.

Article 57 (Duty of Confidentiality) A person who performs or has performed duties under this Act shall not disclose confidential information concerning the management of disaster management resources learned in the course of those duties or use it for purposes other than enforcement of this Act.

Article 58 (Guidance and Supervision) In connection with management of disaster management resources, the Minister of the Interior and Safety and Mayors/Do Governors may guide and supervise national disaster management support enterprises, regional disaster management support enterprises, and national disaster management logistics enterprises within the scope necessary for reliable management and rapid mobilization of disaster management resources.

Article 59 (Reports and Inspections)
(1) Where deemed necessary for enforcement of this Act, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may require any of the following to submit data or reports concerning the management of disaster management resources:
1. National disaster management support enterprises;
2. National disaster management logistics enterprises;
3. Information center operating institutions;
4. The heads of management institutions.
(2) Where deemed necessary for enforcement of this Act, a Mayor/Do Governor may require any of the following to submit data or reports concerning the management of disaster management resources:
1. Persons operating a regional integrated resource management center on behalf of another under Article 45 (3);
2. Regional disaster management support enterprises under the Mayor/Do Governor's jurisdiction;
3. Management institutions within the relevant jurisdiction.
(3) Where it is difficult to achieve the purpose of an investigation through submission of data or reports under paragraphs (1) and (2), the Minister of the Interior and Safety or a Mayor/Do Governor may have relevant public officials enter the relevant business establishments, sales offices, etc. to inspect books, documents, and other objects.
(4) The head of a management institution shall regularly inspect management of disaster management resources as prescribed by Presidential Decree and shall inspect management of disaster management resources under the head's jurisdiction from time to time where a resource management officer, resource receipt and issue officer, or resource utilization officer is replaced or where otherwise necessary.

Article 60 (Hearings) The Minister of the Interior and Safety shall hold a hearing when intending to revoke the designation of an information center operating institution under Article 48.

Article 61 (Delegation and Entrustment of Authority, etc.)
(1) Part of the authority of the Minister of the Interior and Safety under this Act may be delegated to Mayors/Do Governors or the heads of affiliated institutions, or entrusted to the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) The following functions of the Minister of the Interior and Safety under this Act may be entrusted to information center operating institutions, as prescribed by Presidential Decree:
1. Surveys of supply chain management information under Article 7 (1);
2. Requests for submission of data necessary for surveys of supply chain management information under Article 7 (2);
3. Entry of supply chain management information under Article 8 (1);
4. Establishment and operation of the integrated resource management system under Article 46 (1);
5. Requests for submission of data necessary for establishment and operation of the integrated resource management system under Article 46 (2);
6. Provision or disclosure of information in the integrated resource management system under Article 46 (3).

Article 62 (Deeming Persons Public Officials for Application of Penalties) Executives and employees of information center operating institutions shall be deemed public officials for purposes of applying Articles 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act.

CHAPTER IX PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 63 (Penalties)
(1) A person who exports disaster management resources or removes them from the country in violation of Article 15 (1) shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than five years or a fine not exceeding 50 million won.
(2) Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than three years or a fine not exceeding 30 million won:
1. A person who affixes or uses a mark indicating status as a national disaster management support enterprise in violation of Article 9 (3);
2. A person who affixes or uses a mark indicating status as a regional disaster management support enterprise in violation of Article 12 (3);
3. A person who affixes or uses a mark indicating status as a national disaster management logistics enterprise in violation of Article 17 (3);
4. A person who discloses confidential information concerning the management of disaster management resources or uses such confidential information for purposes other than enforcement of this Act, in violation of Article 57.
(3) Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than one year or a fine not exceeding 10 million won:
1. A person who, without just cause, refuses to receive a notice specifying the duties of a national disaster management support enterprise under Article 9 (2), or damages the notice or otherwise impairs its effectiveness;
2. A person who, without just cause, refuses to receive a notice specifying the duties of a regional disaster management support enterprise under Article 12 (2), or damages the notice or otherwise impairs its effectiveness;
3. A person who, without just cause, refuses to receive a notice specifying the duties of a national disaster management logistics enterprise under Article 17 (2), or damages the notice or otherwise impairs its effectiveness;
4. A person who violates, without just cause, a mobilization order of a Mayor/Do Governor under Article 50 (1);
5. A person who violates, without just cause, a mobilization order of the head of the Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters under Article 51 (1);
6. A person who violates, without just cause, a mobilization order of the head of the Central Accident Response Headquarters under Article 52.

Article 64 (Joint Penalty Provisions) Where the representative of a corporation or organization, or an agent, employee, or other worker of a corporation, organization, or individual commits a violation under Article 63 in connection with the business of that corporation, organization, or individual, the corporation, organization, or individual shall also be subject to the fine prescribed in the relevant Article, in addition to punishment of the offender: Provided, That this shall not apply where the corporation, organization, or individual has not neglected due care and supervision in relation to the relevant business to prevent the violation.

Article 65 (Administrative Fines)
(1) Any of the following persons shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 10 million won:
1. A person who fails to submit data or reports under Article 59 (1) and (2), or submits false data or reports;
2. A person who refuses, obstructs, or evades an inspection under Article 59 (3).
(2) Any of the following persons shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding five million won:
1. A person who fails to enter supply chain management information in the integrated resource management system or enters false information in violation of Article 8 (2);
2. A person who uses the name “national disaster management support enterprise” or a similar name in violation of Article 9 (4);
3. A person who uses the name “regional disaster management support enterprise” or a similar name in violation of Article 12 (4);
4. A person who uses the name “national disaster management logistics enterprise” or a similar name in violation of Article 17 (4).
(3) Administrative fines under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be imposed and collected by the Minister of the Interior and Safety or a Mayor/Do Governor, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

ADDENDA <Act No. 19213, 2023.1.17>
